data.title: Timeline
data.tagline: Show a sequence of events in time order
data.description: A timeline works for shipping, approval records, and release history. Choose whether the newest event appears first or last and stay consistent. Dates, labels, and status text carry the meaning; dots and colors only help people scan.

use: A record of events over time
avoid: Use a timeline for items with no meaningful order
Rely on dot color without status text
Pack long, unrelated documents into each event

lessonPractice.title: A ticket detail page records who created, transferred, and closed the ticket and when. All events already happened. How should they appear?

options.label: Use a timeline with one direction and show the person, time, and action for each event
options.feedback: These are historical events with temporal order, so a timeline expresses both sequence and each specific change.

options.label: Use a stepper for Create, Transfer, and Close and let users mark each stage complete
options.feedback: A stepper usually guides work still to be completed, while this page must reconstruct past records and responsibility.

options.label: Use a regular list and sort the actions alphabetically for easier lookup
options.feedback: Alphabetical ordering removes event sequence, so users cannot see how the ticket state changed.

data.agentPrompt: Turn the ticket audit trail into a timeline ordered consistently newest-first or oldest-first. Show actor, time, action, and outcome at every node. Do not present it as pending steps, and test failed transfer and reopened events.
